deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It holds two kinds of draft material from the formalities of Riemann's doctoral defence at Göttingen in December 1851.

(a) Top: two successive drafts of a Latin thesis sentence, continuing the drafting of the 'theses' on the previous page (fol. 98r). In the first draft Riemann begins with 'In vulgari istac functionis determinatae ... definitione', having struck out 'legis notionis' and 'propriae non possumus'. He then recasts it as: 'In vulgaribus functionum complexae quantitatis variabilis determinatarum definitionibus [ubi] notae superfluae inesse mihi videntur' — 'In the usual definitions of (determinate) functions of a complex variable quantity, superfluous characteristics (notae, i.e. logical Merkmale) seem to me to be contained.' He changes 'nobis' to 'mihi'.

The mathematical content behind this thesis is not argued on the page. It is the programme of his dissertation (§1, §20, and the remark on p.16 cited on 98r). There a function w of z = x+iy is defined only by the requirement that dw/dz be independent of the direction of dz, i.e. the Cauchy–Riemann equations. The usual definition demands, in addition, an analytic expression built from 'Grössenoperationen'. Riemann regards that extra requirement as a superfluous Merkmal, and he defers to a later occasion the proof that the two notions coincide (see fol. 99r).

(b) Below the Roman numeral 'I.': repeated drafts of German title-page and announcement wording. Typical phrases are 'Eine Abhandlung von B. Riemann', 'behufs Erlangung der Doctorwürde', 'zu deren öffentlicher Vertheidigung der Verfasser ... ', and 'am 16 Dec 1851', '11 Uhr 30 Min Vormittags'. One stray line reads '1851 Dec 15. 23 30', possibly a time note. This documents the date and time of the public defence: 16 December 1851, 11:30 a.m. That agrees with the known date of Riemann's promotion.

results.what: Thesis that customary definitions of complex functions contain superfluous conditions (an analytic expression), as opposed to Riemann's definition by direction-independence of the derivative
results.modern_name: Definition of holomorphic function via Cauchy–Riemann equations / complex differentiability (vs. Weierstrassian analytic-expression definition)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Inaugural dissertation 1851 (with Cauchy for the C-R equations)

results.what: Drafts of title page / defence announcement: defence on 16 Dec 1851, 11:30 a.m.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds only Latin thesis drafting and title-page wording for the 1851 dissertation defence. The thesis about superfluous 'notae' in the usual definition restates the well-known programme of the dissertation. The drafting history is of mild archival interest only.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); u=re(expand((x+I*y)**3)); v=im(expand((x+I*y)**3)); simplify(diff(u,x)-diff(v,y))==0 and simplify(diff(u,y)+diff(v,x))==0
checkable.asserts: Illustration of the dissertation's defining condition: a function given by an analytic expression, z**3, satisfies the Cauchy–Riemann equations (direction-independence of dw/dz).

transcription_corrections: Second Latin draft should read 'definitionibus' or 'definitione' with 'videntur'/'videatur'. The image shows 'definitione' at the line end, with 'ubi' inserted before 'notae' and 'mihi' written above struck 'nobis'.
'Eine Abhandlung von B Riemann' is correct; the date line reads 'behufs Erlangung der Doctorwürde am 16 Dec 1851'.

The line transcribed 'zur [-Erwerbung der Doctorwürde-]' is uncertain. It appears to begin 'zur' or 'zwei', followed by struck words, and should be marked as illegible rather than given a confident reading.
'1851 Dec 15. 23 30 bestimmt' is plausibly correct as written in the image. It may be a time note ('15. 23 30') rather than part of the title.
The final line is largely illegible ('... Uhr ... Vertheidigung ...'). It likely repeats the defence wording with 'um ... Uhr' and 'mit[?]' above.
